definitions.explanation: A management philosophy that evaluates and rewards employees based on their output and achievements rather than seniority or hours worked.

examples.english: Our company follows a performance-based system.

examples.english: More and more companies are introducing performance-based systems.

examples.english: There are arguments for and against meritocracy, including criticism that it increases employee stress.

notes:
USAGE:
A buzzword in Japanese business since the late 1990s, when companies began moving away from the traditional ⟦{年功序列|ねんこうじょれつ}→年功序列：12532_nenkoujoretsu⟧ (seniority-based) system. Still debated in management circles.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {成果|せいか}{主義|しゅぎ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{導入|どうにゅう}する→導入する：16055_dounyuusuru⟧ (to introduce a performance-based system)
- {成果|せいか}{主義|しゅぎ}{型|がた}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{評価|ひょうか}→評価：03583_hyouka⟧ (performance-based evaluation)
- {成果|せいか}{主義|しゅぎ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{弊害|へいがい}→弊害：09349_heigai⟧ (drawbacks of meritocracy)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{年功序列|ねんこうじょれつ}→年功序列：12532_nenkoujoretsu⟧: seniority system — the traditional Japanese model where pay and rank increase with years of service
- ⟦{実力主義|じつりょくしゅぎ}→実力主義：17836_jitsuryokushugi⟧: meritocracy based on ability — similar but emphasizes skill rather than measurable output
